messages:
Sam: FYI — POC kickoff with FinVault next Tue. They're insisting on BYO-HSM (CloudHSM) + Redwood key-proxy. Need: latency impact, rotation options, and pricing delta by EOD tomorrow. Who can own the answers?
Priya: I can take point on the presales doc. quick q: are they doing per-request sign/encrypt for every user request or establishing session tokens? that changes perf a lot.
Sam: Per-request for user-facing encrypt/signs. low-latency is a blocker for them. also they asked about daily rotation and attestation requirements.
Omar: For per-op proxied HSM calls we typically see an added tail cost depending on region and HSM vendor. ballpark: median +6–12ms, 95th +18–35ms on our current infra with CloudHSM in us-west-2. important caveat: these numbers assume mTLS to HSM + single TCP handshake reuse.
Lena: We ran a quick microbenchmark last month. sample command we used:
```
curl -s -X POST https://kms-proxy.redwood.internal/crypto \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"op":"sign","key_id":"cust-kek-123","payload":"..."}'
```
Result: median 9ms, p95 22ms (us-west-2, private VPC peering to CloudHSM). I can export the raw csv.
Kyle: Pricing note: BYO-HSM POC typically gets an integration/setup fee + per-100k-op surcharge while HSM egress and management add operational cost. For quoting, use: $1,500 one-time integration + $0.025 per 1k proxied ops as a placeholder until finance provides regional pricing. mark as draft.
Priya: For the security questionnaire: we should confirm these points for FinVault — 1) Redwood never has plaintext customer keys (we store only wrapped blobs), 2) HSM holds KEK under customer control, 3) access to HSM admin ops requires 2-person authorization in customer's KMS, 4) we keep audit logs and can provide export. can someone paste the exact Q&A snippets?
Omar: I'll paste short answers for the questionnaire. key points: "Customer-managed keys in HSM; Redwood performs wrapped-key operations, does not export plaintext. Hardware attestation available; we can accept cert chain from vendor. Rotation is customer-triggered or automated via schedule; old key material retained per the customer's retention policy for decrypt-only period"
Priya: Customer asked about 'daily rotation' — are we comfortable supporting 24h rotation with proxied operations (they're concerned about restart/fallback windows)?
Lena: Technically yes. recommended flow for zero-downtime rotation: 1) provision new KEK in HSM, 2) provision wrapped key in Redwood, 3) canary traffic at 5–10% for 30m, 4) full cutover. If they rotate daily we suggest canary window shortened to 5–10m and monitor errors. frequent rotation increases HSM ops (and cost).
Omar: Also note: rotation that re-encrypts large volumes (backfill) is the heavy part. If all operations just use new KEK for new encrypts and keep old KEK for decrypt-only, cost is minimal. full rewrap of existing blobs is expensive.
Sam: FinVault also asked about regional failover — if HSM in us-west-2 is down, what's fallback?
Kyle: Options: 1) multi-region HSM replication (customer-managed) — lowest latency hit but heavier ops; 2) fallback to a Redwood-hosted KMS (requires contractual approval) with clear SLA and different trust model; 3) read-only degrade (deny new encrypts, allow decrypts with cached keys). We should surface these in the SOW and explicitly call out trust and billing differences.
Priya: Action items: Omar to drop questionnaire snippets + attestation steps; Lena to attach latency CSV and brief test instructions; Kyle to create a draft pricing line item; Sam to draft SOW with these options and pass to legal/security for review. timeline: tomorrow EOD for presales packet.
Omar: Snippet for questionnaire (feel free to copy): "Redwood supports customer-managed KEKs in external HSMs. We never persist unwrapped key material. All HSM operations occur over mutually authenticated channels; customers may provide HSM attestation certs. Rotation can be scheduled; we recommend canary-first rollouts for safety"
Lena: Uploaded benchmark CSV to the shared drive: /shared/sales/presales/finvault/kms_latency_usw2.csv (I'll PM link).
sec-bot: Uploaded: redwood_kms_finvault_questionnaire_answers_v1.pdf
Kyle: Draft pricing attached in the drive as well. FYI the $0.025/1k is conservative — finance may push it up slightly for multi-region replication.
Sam: Great — I'll consolidate into a single packet for FinVault and flag out the enterprise blockers: multi-region HA decision, attestation cert exchange, and SOW-approved fallback model. tagging legal and security for review. Thanks all :thumbsup:
